messages:
incident-bot: PAGED @oncall-alex: p95/p99 latency SLO breach for hosted/gpu-shared pool in us-west-2. Alerting tier: sev2. Streaming stalls reported. Metric: p99 gen latency spike to 2.8s (baseline ~0.35s).
oncall-alex: I'm on it. grabbing logs + checking recent deploys. any customer-facing errors?
cs-ellie: we've got a couple of customer reports about long streaming stalls and token drops for chat sessions, some timeouts at 30s. Not widespread but affecting 3 tenants on shared pool.
eng-sre-jamie: seeing increased GPU utilisation on node-gw-12 and node-gw-14, iowait spikes on NVMe -> possible IO contention. Also multiple cgroup throttles fired.
mlops-ravi: which models were active? could be a heavy quantized decoder with large KV cache. pulling model-metrics now.
infra-maya: quick mitigation: recommend cordon node-gw-14 from autoscaler, migrate active sessions off those nodes to dedicated pool or other racks. I'll prepare drain script.
oncall-alex: Do we have capacity to shift tenants to dedicated? Which ones? cs-ellie can you ID impacted tenants and whether they have Dedicated contracts?
cs-ellie: Tenant IDs: T-8342 (startup), T-9121 (enterprise-basic), T-7003 (pilot). T-9121 has Dedicated on request but not active. They are sensitive; want frequent updates.
eng-sre-jamie: Quick check: top procs on gw-14 are multi-tenant batch jobs + a few streaming sessions. cgroups show blkio.weight changes and blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes. NVMe latency correlates with GPU kernel run times. Suspect noisy neighbor IO saturation.
pm-lena: any risk of SLA breach for enterprise customers? need clear statement for comms.
oncall-alex: We have p95 > SLO for overall pool; customer-facing SLAs may be impacted for those tenants. cs-ellie please prepare an incident message for affected customers.
infra-maya: Running quick mitigation: I will temporarily reduce max concurrent sessions per instance on gw-12/gw-14 to 4 (from 8) via reroute config, and evict non-critical batch jobs. Command used: 
```
# set max_conns for pool
redwoodctl pool update gpu-shared --max-conns 4 --region us-west-2
# evict batch label
redwoodctl job evict --label "batch" --nodes gw-12,gw-14
```
mlops-ravi: also enabling KV cache sharing for active chat sessions to reduce repeated token recomputation. Patching inference config: 
```
inference.config.kv_cache.shared = true
inference.config.batching.max_batch_size = 16
```
oncall-alex: running drain on gw-14 now: moving live sessions with graceful handoff (streaming support in progress). Expect some dropped streams during handoff but minimized.
eng-sre-jamie: logs show cgroup blkio.throttle_io_service_bytes exceeded threshold at 18:43:02; throttling persisted ~120s. After evict and pool update, NVMe latency drops from 12ms -> 2.5ms and p99 falls back to ~0.5s.
incident-bot: incident update posted to #incidents: "Latency spike due to IO contention on shared GPU pool; mitigation in progress."
cs-ellie: customer updates sent to T-8342 and T-7003. Draft for T-9121 pending approval (sensitive).
pm-lena: good. Add note to postmortem: consider per-tenant IO isolation and default blkio.weight tuning. Also track which models cause persistent KV churn.
mlops-ravi: on model side, flagging model 'redwood/large-chat-v2' as high-io; adding quantization + KV persistence recommendations to Optimize.
eng-sre-jamie: tagging metrics to follow for 30m: p95, p99, NVMe lat, cgroup throttle count, GPU utilization.
oncall-alex: handing off to eng-sre-jamie for monitoring and verification. I'm logging details in PagerDuty. If anything regresses ping me.
oncall-alex: rest of infra: please avoid rolling restarts in us-west-2 for 30m to not perturb migration.
eng-sre-jamie: monitoring looks stable for 20m; p99 ~0.48s, p95 ~0.22s. No further cgroup throttle events. NVMe latency steady.
infra-maya: completed de-cordon of gw-14, but left reduced max_conns until business hour end. Plan: revert max_conns tomorrow unless further issues.
cs-ellie: final customer messages queued. No loss of persisted data; streaming clients experienced short stalls during handoff window (~3-6s).
pm-lena: thanks team. We'll schedule a postmortem and mitigation backlog item: per-tenant IO limits, smarter eviction (batch vs streaming), and autoscaler sensitivity to blkio metrics.
eng-sre-jamie: assigning follow-ups: JIRA INF-4821 (blkio-weight tuning), INF-4822 (streaming handoff improvements), INF-4823 (monitoring for cgroup throttle).
oncall-alex: closing handoff. If any regression alerting triggers, PD will repage. Good job. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: incident marked as mitigated (sev2 -> monitoring)."
